title: LINQ in Depth
summary: The rest of LINQ - query syntax and how it maps to methods, joining two sequences with Join and GroupJoin, flattening with SelectMany, Aggregate, Zip, Chunk and the By methods, ToLookup, set operations, and the deferred execution rules that decide when a query actually runs.

cards.q: What is the difference between `Join` and `GroupJoin`?
cards.a:
`Join` drops items with no match; `GroupJoin` keeps them

`Join` gives one result per matching pair, an inner join. `GroupJoin` gives one result per item of the first sequence with all its matches, possibly none.

cards.q: Why might a LINQ query run more slowly than expected inside a loop?
cards.a:
Deferred queries run again every time they are enumerated; `ToList()` runs them once

A query is a recipe, not a result. Enumerating it inside a loop repeats all the work each time unless the results are stored.

cards.q: numbers.Where(n => n > 2) is assigned to q, then 5 is added to numbers. What does q.Count() count?
cards.a:
every number above 2, including the 5

The query is deferred, so it runs when Count is called and sees the current list.
